recognize_zh: 中央小淋巴球的核明顯比多數紅血球大，紅血球偏小且中央淡染區擴大（hypochromia），並夾雜細長的鉛筆狀細胞（pencil cells），符合小球性低色素紅血球（microcytosis）。
features: Red cells are smaller than the nucleus of the adjacent small lymphocyte (microcytosis)
Widened central pallor in many red cells (hypochromia)
Anisopoikilocytosis with elongated pencil cells and occasional teardrop forms
A neutrophil and a small lymphocyte provide size reference
Platelets appear numerous in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells that are predominantly smaller than the nucleus of a small lymphocyte, with increased central pallor. There is moderate anisopoikilocytosis including elongated pencil cells and occasional teardrop forms. Platelets appear increased in number. No basophilic stippling or target cells are prominent. Findings are consistent with microcytic, hypochromic anemia; the pencil cells and apparent thrombocytosis favor iron deficiency, to be confirmed with iron studies.

ddx.vs: Thalassemia trait tends to show target cells and basophilic stippling with a normal RDW and high red cell count, whereas pencil cells and marked anisocytosis favor iron deficiency; iron studies and hemoglobin analysis separate them.
Anemia of chronic disease is usually normocytic or mildly microcytic with less poikilocytosis; ferritin and iron-binding capacity distinguish them.
Sideroblastic anemia often shows a dimorphic population with Pappenheimer bodies and requires ring sideroblasts on marrow iron stain.
